lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 29
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: What She Wanted
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo moved while the others were still listening to the knock that had answered from beneath the City.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek was staring at the new ridge rising under the skin of his palm. Ninsun was still translating the last line that had carved itself into the wall. BAH-lahg stood between them and the man in the alcove with the patient stillness of someone who had already decided the ground was wrong. For a few breaths no one watched her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She had spent her whole life noticing the exact moment when attention slipped. She used it the way other people used doors.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The passage past the alcove narrowed at once. Walls pressed close enough that her shoulders brushed both sides. The torchlight behind her thinned, then vanished. She kept walking until the voices were gone, swallowed by stone the way everything in this place eventually got swallowed, and only then let herself stop.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She did not take the journal. She took the question that had been sitting behind her teeth since the gatekeeper first said the word Payment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: What will I possess when I leave this place?
lines.note: Internal thought; intimate, not voiced aloud.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She did not speak it aloud. She simply held the thought the way she had once held a lockpick—firm, quiet, without apology—and waited to see whether the City would answer a request that had never been asked of it in words.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The air changed first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stone against her back went warm, then soft, then absent. Blue sky opened overhead, so bright it hurt. She was walking through a gate of white stone veined with gold. Bronze doors stood open. Servants bowed. Above the entrance, cut deep enough to last a thousand years, her own name:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: ENHEDU.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The air smelled of clean cistern water. Caravans rolled past loaded with lapis and ivory. Men who had once looked through her now waited in line, hats in hand. A ring slid onto her finger, cool at first and then warm. A house north of the river. Walls high enough to keep the starving world outside where it belonged.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A woman stood in the doorway of that house. For one strange second en-HEH-doo did not recognize her—older, softer, safe in a way that felt like a foreign language. Then she understood. It was her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Coin was the one thing in the world that never pretended to love you first. It had all led here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo smiled.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then, somewhere behind her ribs, everything went quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The change arrived so fast she almost missed it under the noise of her own triumph. She was still standing in the palace. She could still see the gold, still price it out of habit—the ring worth a season's rent, the vase worth a man's life if sold to the right buyer. She knew the house was beautiful. She knew the people around her were powerful.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She felt none of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The fire that had carried her through every bad deal and every worse night—the thing that had kept her moving when moving was the only thing keeping her fed—had simply gone out, like someone had reached into her chest and pinched the wick.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The vision folded.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was back in the narrow dark of the passage, a small golden figurine solid and cold in her open hand. She knew exactly what it was worth. She knew exactly how many throats would be cut for it. She looked at it the way she would look at a chipped cup.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing there worth the looking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That was when Zeek found her. He appeared at the far end of the passage without sound, the way everything in this place had learned to move. His eyes went from the figurine to her face. Something in her expression told him more than either object did.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: en-HEH-doo?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned toward him. For the first time since he had known her, she looked lost, and she hated that he was the one who got to see it.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I know this matters,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said, and held out the figurine like proof.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took it, turned it once in the torchlight. Even here, in a place that swallowed light whole, the gold seemed to drink the dark rather than push it back.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Where did you get this?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I don't remember.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You don't remember taking it?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I remember the room.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her gaze slid past him into the dark.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I remember wanting it.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Wanting what?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Everything.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She looked down at her own empty hands as if they belonged to someone else.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I saw the life I wanted. Money. A house. People who couldn't decide I was worthless because they'd never been able to afford me in the first place.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her voice stayed level. Whatever was underneath it had gone completely flat.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: And then I had it.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I don't care.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words sat between them, ugly and small.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's eyes moved to the mark on his own palm, still faintly raised where the knock had pressed outward from inside the skin.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: What did you ask?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: What will I possess when I leave this place.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked at her for a long moment.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You waited for it to ask,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I asked first.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg and Ninsun arrived a minute later, drawn by the sound of voices carrying down the passage. BAH-lahg stopped when he saw the figurine. Ninsun's face lit with instinctive scholarly hunger—then died the moment she saw en-HEH-doo's expression underneath it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What happened?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo passed her the figurine without a word.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun turned it over, ran a thumb along the tooling.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This is extraordinarily valuable.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Yes.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You don't seem pleased.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo's mouth twitched, not quite a smile.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I know.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked between the three of them, working through it the way he worked through everything—one slow, honest step at a time.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So you got what you wanted.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Yes.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then what's the problem? Sell it. Buy the house. Be done with it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: BAH-lahg.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's voice had an edge.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I'm asking a real question.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He wasn't being cruel. That was the worst part—he genuinely didn't see it yet, and en-HEH-doo found she couldn't even be angry at him for that, because an hour ago she wouldn't have seen it either.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You wanted things. Now you have one. Isn't that the whole point of wanting?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo looked at the figurine in Ninsun's hands—gold enough to have bought her out of every bad year she had ever lived—and felt exactly nothing reach for it.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It was,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg frowned, sensing he had missed something without being able to name it, and let the silence do what his questions could not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Somewhere beyond the alcove the triple knock began again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three times.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo turned toward the sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She did not reach for her knife.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She did not reach for the gold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She simply stood there while the City waited to see what else she no longer cared enough to protect.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They moved in uneasy silence after en-HEH-doo's change.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nobody suggested asking the City another question. Not even en-HEH-doo, who carried the golden figurine wrapped in cloth the way a man carries a stone in his boot—aware of it with every step, unable to feel anything about it. She knew it was valuable. She remembered wanting it. That was all that remained of the wanting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The passage opened into a chamber with three doors, identical in size and nothing alike in what waited beyond them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first opened onto a sunlit courtyard. Trees heavy with leaves. Water moving somewhere out of sight. Birds cut through the branches. Laughter drifted from beyond the doorway, easy and unhurried, the sound of people who had never once had to calculate the weight of anything. Beautiful. Completely impossible. They were too deep beneath the First City for sunlight to exist at all, let alone this much of it—warm and gold and entirely unbothered by the stone pressing down from above.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second door opened onto a sheer drop into blackness. No floor beyond the threshold. No far wall. No bottom that torchlight or imagination could find. The dark simply continued, patient as everything else in this place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third showed the corridor they were already standing in—empty. No Zeek. No BAH-lahg. No en-HEH-doo. No Ninsun. The same stretch of stone reaching away into the distance, untouched and silent, as though the four of them had never set foot in it at all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stared at the third door longest.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't like that one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo glanced at him. Some of her old dryness surfaced, thinner than before.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You don't like the one showing us exactly what we are.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't like the one showing us nothing.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That's because you have simple tastes.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His hand drifted toward his axe.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Enough,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said. She stood between the three doorways, studying the carvings above each one—symbols she had already copied twice, comparing them against every fragment of the City's language she had catalogued. None of it matched. When she began to trace one familiar root with her stylus, the mark on the parchment went blank under the tip. She stared at the empty space for a long moment, then closed the scroll without comment.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The inscriptions aren't telling us which door to take.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Then what are they telling us?

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She lifted the compass instead. The needle swung from the courtyard to the black drop to the empty corridor and back again, circling once before settling—pointing straight down, through the floor, toward nothing any of them could name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark on Zeek's palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stepped toward the third door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg caught his arm.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That one shows us gone.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words of the man who had refused returned without invitation: That threshold does not ask. It only records the answer you already gave by arriving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek set his foot on the threshold of the empty corridor.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The floor held.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took another step.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind him the others waited. en-HEH-doo watched with the flat attention of someone who no longer calculated odds the way she once had. Ninsun's stylus hovered over parchment that had nowhere useful left to write. BAH-lahg's grip on the axe was white-knuckled and certain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked back once.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Stay behind me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stepped fully through.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor beyond was the same corridor they had left. The same oily stone. The same slow drip of water that measured no hours anyone recognized. For three paces nothing changed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On the fourth the lesson was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not the memory of his father.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not the sound of the old man's voice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not the desert nights spent learning which stones would hold and which would open.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Only the specific knowledge of how to test a floor—the exact sequence of weight and listening and the small adjustments of the ankle that had once been as automatic as breathing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He knew that something important had been taken. He could feel the absence the way he felt the mark under the linen. He knew it had once been the difference between walking and falling. The exact edges of the missing thing were already going soft, the way a word goes soft in the mouth right before it is lost entirely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His body still remembered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His hand still knew how to test the next stone. His feet still knew where not to fall. The lesson remained somewhere the City had not yet reached—buried in muscle and instinct too deep for the current extraction to dig out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stood in the corridor and waited for the others.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg came first, then Ninsun, then en-HEH-doo. None of them spoke. The three doors behind them folded shut without a sound, as though the chamber had never held more than one choice to begin with.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From somewhere ahead, deeper than the corridor they now occupied, three measured knocks answered the mark.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept walking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind him en-HEH-doo carried the gold she no longer wanted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beside him Ninsun carried symbols that no longer yielded meaning.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His body still knew which stones would hold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek no longer knew what it was listening for.
